drafted_from: tool row in tools/keep-a-video-packaging-ledger/tool-rows.json, do-work/ingest_channel_intake.py and test/test_channel_intake_append_new.py (run on its fixture)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Add the two videos I reviewed in admission/batch to my packaging ledger under source key ch-example-videos, as a later batch (append new), working in /work/example-channel." It reads the tool's row, then runs ingest_channel_intake.py on your computer and tells you how many rows the ledger has now.
no_lists_because: It keeps no Trillion list: the ledger is a JSON Lines file in the person's own working folder, one row per video, and the tool reads and writes files there.
instructions: 1. Put the batch's files in your working folder (root): an intake manifest (INTAKE.json), the channel catalog (CATALOG.json), the review record (REVIEW.json), and the coverage files the ledger keeps beside it (COVERAGE-REPORT.json, SOURCE-COVERAGE.json).

2. Say which source key the batch goes under. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:add-reviewed-videos-to-a-packaging-ledger}, checks blake3 is installed (python3 -c 'import blake3') and runs its `run` command from the Workshop checkout; add --append-new when the source key already has rows.
3. Read the last JSON line it prints: videos, rows_before, rows_after, all_old_non_target_rows_preserved, source_key and operation; the read-back file at --readback lists the ids added.
4. Check the result with tool:check-a-packaging-intake-against-the-ledger, using a copy of the ledger made before you ran this.

worked_examples.title: Append two reviewed videos to a ledger of four rows
worked_examples.ask: Add the two videos I reviewed in admission/batch to my packaging ledger under source key ch-example-videos, as a later batch.
worked_examples.given: From tools/keep-a-video-packaging-ledger/test/test_channel_intake_append_new.py (test_second_batch_appends_once_and_preserves_all_prior_lines), which I ran on its fixture to observe the output. Command: python3 -I tools/keep-a-video-packaging-ledger/do-work/ingest_channel_intake.py --root /work/example-channel --ledger /work/example-channel/VIDEO-PACKAGING.jsonl --source-key ch-example-videos --intake /work/example-channel/admission/batch/INTAKE.json --channel-catalog /work/example-channel/admission/batch/CATALOG.json --review /work/example-channel/admission/batch/REVIEW.json --coverage /work/example-channel/COVERAGE-REPORT.json --source-coverage /work/example-channel/SOURCE-COVERAGE.json --readback /work/example-channel/admission/batch/READBACK.json --append-new. The ledger holds 3 rows of source key ch-example-videos (old-video-1 to 3) and 1 row of another key; the batch is new-video-1 and new-video-2, each with a metadata file, a caption file and a thumbnail image.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"videos": 2, "rows_before": 4, "rows_after": 6, "all_old_non_target_rows_preserved": true, "source_key": "ch-example-videos", "operation": "append-new"} The first four ledger lines are byte for byte as they were; two rows follow, each pinning the metadata, image and caption files by BLAKE3 and holding the opening hook as a caption file, event index 0 and span 1.0 to 3.0 seconds with caption_text_copied false. Running the same command again changes no ledger byte and adds no second batch to the coverage files.
